text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 SLO breach detected for router/eu-west-2. Streaming stalls observed, tail latency spike > 3s. Paging oncall. Source: routing metrics pipeline.

alex: oncall here. pulling graphs now — which customers are affected?

jen: looking at telemetry — p95 ~ 600ms, p99 ~ 3.4s for text-gen paths. Streaming sessions show stall windows around 10:12-10:18 UTC. Error budget burn started ~10:11.

mohit: initial signal looks like misrouting to a small set of hot shards + a policy roll we pushed 09:55 that tweaked `router.affinity.weight` for eu-west-2. suspect hot partitioning + sticky affinity increase.

ryan: any customer-impacting errors? Simone pls?

simone: Support: 3 customers opened tickets complaining about slow responses and streaming timeouts. Two are multi-region but defaulting to eu-west-2. No 5xxs, just high latency/timeouts on stream frames.

lina: I can run a quick traffic split away from eu-west-2 to relieve tail if we want manual mitigation.

alex: do it. We need to reduce p99 ASAP. Start with 20% shift to fallback region (eu-central-1). Notify customers after stabilization.

lina: running command now:```bash
rbctl traffic shift --from=eu-west-2 --to=eu-central-1 --percent=20 --dry-run=false
```

incident-bot: Command accepted: shift job id 7421 queued.

jen: throwing up a short-lived dashboard: link: https://dash/redwood/incidents/1839999999 (mock). watching p99.

mohit: can someone fetch the routing policy diff from 09:55? I pushed a small heuristic change that increases local affinity weight when SLA tier=gold. suspect the heuristic misclassified a set of keys as gold due to telemetry bug.

alex: @mohit please paste the diff. If it's clearly risky we can roll back.

mohit: paste:```diff
--- routing-policy@09:50
+++ routing-policy@09:55
@@
- if (session.metadata.sla_tier == 'gold') weight += 0.15
+ if (session.metadata.sla_tier == 'gold' || session.metadata.region == 'eu-west-2') weight += 0.15
```
This was intended to favor local for gold, but the `|| region==eu-west-2` was added to bias local in euw2 for perf — probably overshot and created hot fanout.

jen: that additional clause definitely increases affinity for many keys in euw2. That can create hot partitions if top keys concentrate.

ryan: timeline check — policy was rolled at 09:55, p99 started at 10:11. matches.

lina: traffic shift job 7421 started. current shift: 20% -> eu-central-1. Observing immediate drop in incoming load to top 10 shards (heatmap).

simone: tickets: customers A and C reported streaming stalls; customer B is experiencing degraded latency but no timeouts yet. Filed for SOC and CS heads.

alex: good. plan: 1) stabilize with staged traffic shift to 50% if p99 doesn't recover 2) revert policy 09:55 3) run controlled roll-forward with canary checks.

mohit: agree. I've queued an immediate rollback for policy:```bash
configctl rollback routing-policy --to=09:50 --reason="hot-affinity bug"
```

incident-bot: Rollback job 7422 submitted. ETA ~30s for propagation.

jen: p99 at 2.2s now (after 20% shift + in-flight rollback). still above target but trending down. p95 steady ~450ms.

lina: bumping shift to 40% as a precaution:```bash
rbctl traffic shift --from=eu-west-2 --to=eu-central-1 --percent=40
```

mohit: rollback finished. Confirming routing policy is at 09:50. Diff gone.

jen: p99 dropped to 1.1s within 90s of rollback + 40% shift. streaming frame rate recovered, stall events dropping.

simone: updating customer tickets: "We identified a routing policy change that increased local affinity in eu-west-2 causing hot partitions. We've rolled that back and shifted traffic to eu-central-1 to mitigate. Engineers are monitoring and we'll follow up with a postmortem." :white_check_mark:

ryan: thanks team. Do we want to keep 40% shift until we finish a safe canary? Or revert shift as rollback should fix hot partitions?

mohit: I recommend holding at 30-40% for 10 minutes to ensure hot-resets clear caches. The affinity change likely created heavy KV cache pressure; giving the system a chance to rebalance.

alex: hold at 35% then gradually go to 0% over 20 minutes. lina pls set ramp schedule.

lina: setting ramp: 35% hold for 10m, then -10% every 5m. Command:```bash
rbctl traffic ramp --from=eu-west-2 --to=eu-central-1 --start=35 --hold=10m --step=-10 --step-interval=5m
```

incident-bot: Ramp job 7425 created. Alerts will suppress transient alarms for 15m to avoid noise.

jen: note: streaming SLOs p99s are still not fully back to baseline for a handful of legacy shards; I'll create a quick heatmap and add to the postmortem data.

mohit: follow-up action: revert the `region == 'eu-west-2'` clause from the heuristic permanently. I'll open PR with tests that simulate shard concentration.

ryan: add an eval that checks for top-key concentration before applying local-bias — might avoid this in future.

simone: CS communicated a summary to affected customers. They want an ETA for full normalization. Can we commit to <2h?

alex: tentative yes. If p99 stays <1.2s and no regressions in 30m, we'll start gradual traffic return.

lina: monitoring shows traffic now evenly redistributed per plan and background eviction rates returning to normal.

jen: creating incident thread and p99/p95 graphs for postmortem. Will include timelines, routing diffs, customer ticket ids.

mohit: PR created to remove region clause and add canary guard: https://git/redwood/routing/pull/987 (mock).

alex: thanks. Wrapping up: at 10:42 UTC we observed stable p99 ~1.05s. Keeping ramp job active. Postmortem assigned to eng-runtime and SRE.

simone: I'll follow up with customers with the timeline and next steps.

ryan: good postmortem action items: testing for heavy-key skew, canary heuristics, playbook updates for traffic shift.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status -> mitigated. suppressing active paging. Please transition to postmortem channel when ready. :tada:

alex: thanks all. closing handoff to postmortem authors. :thumbsup:
